t: Listen to a talk in a geology class.
Geologists sort rocks into three groups based on how they form.
Igneous rocks form when melted rock, called magma, cools and hardens.
The size of the crystals tells you how fast the magma cooled: slow cooling deep underground gives large crystals, while fast cooling at the surface gives tiny ones.
Small particles, like sand or mud, settle in layers, and over time those layers are pressed together.
Because the layers build up slowly, sedimentary rocks are where we usually find fossils.
Finally, metamorphic rocks are existing rocks that have been changed by intense heat and pressure, without melting.
Marble, for instance, forms when limestone is changed in this way.
